views.evidence: Sunflower silhouette and bee-to-flower scale are plausible. Petals repeat a narrow spear shape and similar radial spacing; the disk has conspicuously uniform concentric elements. Grass reads as scattered angular strips on flat ground. Bee anatomy is too small here to assess finer details.

Striped abdomen, hairy thorax, antennae and pollen load identify a honeybee clearly. Wings appear opaque white with dark drawn veins instead of translucent membranes. Thorax hair resembles uniformly distributed stiff needles; leg segments resemble smooth rods. The sunflower disk is a field of oversized hollow-ended pegs, and petals show stretched parallel texture streaks.

Three legs on each side are distinguishable, and the body clears the flower without an obvious major penetration. Distal feet overlap dark florets, making exact support contact difficult to resolve. The frontal head looks like a broad flat shield, with weak compound-eye definition. Bilaterally raised white wings and repetitive peg florets weaken realism.

Body volumes, six segmented legs and thin wing outlines are legible without obvious extreme stretching or detached limbs. Dense overlapping lines obscure wing-root attachment and thorax junctions. The flower disk remains shaded rather than exposing its mesh, limiting inspection of foot-to-floret intersections.

repairs: Replace the oversized hollow peg florets with smaller, varied botanical forms; break up their uniform height and concentric repetition.
Make wings translucent with subtle reflections, finer veins and distinct overlapping forewing/hindwing silhouettes.
Refine the head into rounded chitin volumes with clearly differentiated compound eyes; taper articulated legs and resolve tarsi against individual florets.
Vary hair length, direction and density, reducing the uniform needle-like appearance.
Introduce petal curvature, overlap and shape variation; reduce stretched texture streaks and improve grass grounding.
Improve wireframe visibility at wing roots and foot contacts, including the flower geometry needed to inspect intersections.
